thread:
sanjay: Heads-up — we're seeing a p99 latency regression for the newly onboarded ceres model for long-context requests (>32k tokens). p95 is OK but p99 jumped from ~420ms to ~1.0s over the last 2 hours. @ian can you take a look? :eyes:
ian: On it. Any repro samples or request IDs?
sanjay: Customer sent request_id=cere-req-20260317-9a2f. Payload is a 40k token doc + generation. I'll paste a minimal repro below.
anna: Adding the customer note — they reported timeouts and retries spiking. Several 5xx downstreams observed.
ian: Quick check: ops metrics show an increase in KV-cache misses for ceres nodepool-3 around 18:24 UTC. Also memory pressure on some GPUs bumped slightly, but not out of bounds. ops-bot: autoscaler triggered +2 nodes at 18:27 UTC due to backlog.
jess: Paging runtime oncall. I'm seeing a cluster-level tail at p99 for "generate" route specifically to model:ceres:v1 with long_seq.
tiago: Can you paste the curl repro? I'll try locally against staging.
sanjay: repro curl (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"model":"ceres:v1","input":"<40k tokens here>","max_tokens":512}'
```
ian: Ran similar locally in canary — reproduced p99 bump. I see spikes during KV cache population step where sequence_len > 16k. The runtime falls back to a slow path for KV layout creation. Stack shows repeated memcpy on host pinned path.
sanjay: That matches customer trace. They hit 1.1s p99 and several client retries. Billing-bot: Affected requests >1000 in last 3 hours across 8 customers.
tiago: Hypothesis: tokenizer/subword changes from the ceres tokenizer created more subtoken fragmentation so effective sequence length for KV indexing is higher. Could be combined with our current chunking heuristic.
ian: Agree. Two parallel likely causes: tokenizer causing different bpe splits, and runtime threshold misdetecting long-seq fastpath -> falling back.
jess: Mitigation options? We need a low-risk mitigation for hosted customers ASAP.
ian: Short-term: enable strict KV prefetch for ceres canary to warm caches (reduce miss storms) + route long_seq requests to a fallback model variant ceres:compat-v1 that uses legacy tokenizer and same weights. I can flip routing within 15m.
tiago: Could also change tokenization config on the canary to use byte-level normalizer to match older counts; that is less risky than full rollback.
sanjay: Customer impact severity: high for interactive workflows. Recommend routing affected customers to fallback variant now while we triage.
anna: I'll coordinate with CS to notify customers and pause auto-retries on client side.
ian: Quick patch plan: 1) adjust runtime sequence threshold from 16k->24k for ceres to avoid slow path fallback; 2) roll routing rule to fallback variant for long inputs; 3) schedule tokenizer parity check and token count diff analysis.
jess: Any risk with raising threshold? Could increase memory usage. We need to monitor KV memory and OOMs.
ian: Aware. I'll monitor and set an auto-rollback if memory > 85% on pool. ops-bot: created incident incident-ceres-kv-179900 with paging and alerting hooks.
tiago: For repro automation, here's a tiny python snippet to hit staging repeatedly with large input (use with rate limit):
```
import requests
s = 'word ' * 40000
for i in range(20):
  r = requests.post('https://staging.api.redwood/v1/generate', json={'model':'ceres:v1','input':s,'max_tokens':64}, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer ...'})
  print(i, r.status_code, len(r.content))
```
sanjay: Good — I'm dropping the sample payload into the support ticket.
anna: CS note drafted and customer notified that we're routing to fallback and investigating.
billing-bot: Noted: affected customers flagged for credit if impact confirmed.
ian: Actioning routing change now. Will flip to ceres:compat-v1 for requests where input_tokens > 16k.
ian: Done — routing rule applied at 18:45 UTC. Real-time metrics show p99 for the route dropped from ~1.0s to ~470ms within 5m.
jess: Nice mitigation. Keep an eye on memory.
ian: Memory climb observed +6% on pool-3 after warm cache. Still below 80%. No OOMs. ops-bot: autoscaler scaled down 1 node at 19:05 UTC.
tiago: I'll run tokenizer diff job to quantify token count delta across 500 sample inputs. Results ETA 2 hours.
sanjay: Next steps: 1) keep routing fallback in place for customers until tokenizer parity is confirmed or runtime fix landed. 2) runtime team to prepare a patch to avoid slowpath for legitimate fastpath cases (IAN). 3) CS to follow-up with customer and offer credits if needed (ANNA).
anna: Acknowledged. I'll schedule a postmortem update for tomorrow.
ian: Will open PR with threshold fix and unit tests. PR: https://git.internal.redwood/p/r/ceres-kv-threshold (WIP).
jess: Thanks all. If anything spikes again tag with incident-ceres-kv-179900. We can revert routing if memory behaves poorly. :thumbsup:
